hello.text: The sanctuary asks no oath of its guests. Here you can rest, speak privately, or release Mara’s soul.

choices.text: Talk with Seris about her gifts.
Talk with Seris about the people in the ledger.
Talk with Seris about using charm.
Entrust the other names to the sanctuary.

gifts.speaker: seris
gifts.text: My blood gives me ways to soften another person’s resistance. Succubus Spittle works through brief contact; sometimes it opens a conversation that would otherwise close. The cloud can let us pass living guards. Neither gift tells me whether I should use it. If I use someone’s trust as a tool, I must answer for that choice. You can ask me to try at marked conversations and guard approaches; persuasion and evidence remain alternatives.

freedom.speaker: seris
freedom.text: I used to think the kindest cage was almost a home. Rowan taught me what that sounded like from inside. I want him beside me. I want him free more. If those wishes cannot both be true, I know which one I must let go. I am afraid that saying it will be easier than doing it.

release.text: You open the lantern without demanding payment, service or testimony. Mara steps into the sanctuary’s light. “I remember the river,” she says. “Give me a little time.” She goes to the empty chair near the north wall. Speak with her when she is ready.

names.speaker: oren
names.text: We will follow these names. You have given us directions, not ownership. Some may refuse our help. We will listen.

past.speaker: seris
past.text: I used to keep two ledgers. One for the archlord, one for myself. In his I wrote the debts. In mine I wrote names, children, places people wanted to see again. I told myself remembering was resistance. Sometimes it was. Sometimes it was a way to feel less guilty while obeying. The second ledger is useful now because it can guide us back. It does not make the first one disappear.

choices.text: Restitution begins with what the victims need.
Was there ever a time you refused?

victims.speaker: seris
victims.text: Then let them tell us. Mara may never want to see me again. I can still make sure she has somewhere to live. I can give evidence against the collectors. I can return what I took. None of that requires her to call me good.

refusal.speaker: seris
refusal.text: Once. A girl had inherited a debt her father never knew he carried. I hid her beyond the boundary. The archlord ordered me to find her, and the mark made every road feel like fire except the one that led to her. I learned to walk that road very slowly. She escaped while I was still learning how to bear it. That was the first time I understood that resisting an order could be a long series of small decisions, not one heroic moment.

charm.speaker: seris
charm.text: It was easier when he smiled. That is what frightens me. I could call the result necessary and stop asking whose choice I borrowed. Getting a clue is not the same as earning trust.

choices.text: Use evidence and persuasion when there is another route.
The power can be useful, but we must own its consequences.

restraint.speaker: seris
restraint.text: Then let us leave some doors closed until we can open them honestly.

accountability.speaker: seris
accountability.text: Then no calling a compelled confidence friendship. No asking the court to treat it as free testimony. And no using it on Rowan to make this less painful.
